title: pi-simple-sri case bank, format 1
description: The cases of a directional improvement or of a defect, as a file a user writes. One format, two profiles chosen by the invocation that reads it -- baseline (which may declare a rubric) and origin (which requires an origin and forbids a rubric) -- and the file carries no discriminator: a bank that is not there still has to be read as one of the two, so the profile is an argument and not a field. The relation between the profile and the fields is the one thing this contract cannot express: JSON Schema cannot tie the presence of one property to the value of another without if/then/oneOf, and the shape stays flat on purpose. src/case-bank.ts is therefore the authority on which profile accepts which fields, and test/unit/case-bank.test.ts validates the same fixtures with both readers. Every level sets additionalProperties: false, so a bank with a misspelled field is refused by name. A change of the shape or of the meaning of a field already declared here is a new format, with a new `format` const.

format.description: The versioned id of the format. A bank of another version is a different contract: src/case-bank.ts refuses it whole instead of reading it as this one with fields missing.

description.description: For humans. It never enters a prompt, and an empty one is accepted: it says nothing, which is what the absence of the key would say too.

rubric.description: The criterion the judge applies to every case of this bank, verbatim. Only the baseline profile accepts it: a defect has an observable truth, and a rubric would leave the judge deciding something the artifact already says.

origin.description: The artifact the defect came from. Required by the origin profile and forbidden by the baseline one, a relation this contract does not express (see the description of the format). The path travels as it was written: the reader neither resolves it nor reads the file, and the flow that reads a defect fails closed before spending when the artifact is not there.

kind.description: How the defect was found, the same two values evidence.items.origin.kind declares in decision@1.

excerpt.description: The entry that does not hold, at the length an evidence excerpt is kept (src/evidence.ts).

cases.description: The cases the gate replays. Two is the floor of Q23: with fewer, the paired replay cannot tell a candidate from the incumbent. The ids are unique, and that rule lives in src/case-bank.ts because JSON Schema has no keyword for it.

id.description: The coordinate of the case in the record and in checkFailures, which is why it is a slug: lowercase letters and digits joined by single hyphens.

prompt.description: The prompt of the replay. The runner prepends /skill:<name> and a space to it, the way it does for a replay item of an M1 diagnosis.

checks.description: What the final answer of the replayed turn has to satisfy. Every check has to pass (AND): an OR is two cases, because the rule of the gate is unanimity between cases. Which of value and pattern a check needs follows from its kind, and JSON Schema ties no property to another, so src/checks.ts validates that pair and is the one place a check is executed.
